cases.question: I'm looking for large-cap value stocks — high free cash flow yield — that are coming out of a long volatility squeeze and starting to move up.
cases.result_summary: count=40 (universe 1139). Large/mega caps, high FCF yield, in a squeeze with price rising (resolving up). Top: ADBE, BMY, CM, CME, IBKR, RY, TMUS, USB.
cases.reason: High-FCF-yield value leg intersected with a real volatility-compression (ttm_squeeze) + upward-resolution qualifier, large-cap scoped. Required retry: the schema-listed pattern 'squeeze' 400s; find_tasignal's #1 'ttm_squeeze' is the accepted token.

defects.desc: Executor rejects the pattern token 'squeeze' with HTTP 400 even though the TaSignal schema enum explicitly lists 'squeeze'. Only 'ttm_squeeze' (find_tasignal's rank-1) is accepted — a resolver/schema-vs-executor vocabulary mismatch.

cases.question: หุ้นจีนตัวเล็กที่กำไรโต แต่ราคาลงมา 30% แล้ว และตอนนี้ RSI รีเซ็ตต่ำกว่า 40 มีตัวไหนบ้าง
cases.result_summary: count=2. China small caps with earnings growth (net_income CAGR) + ~30% drop + oversold RSI: 600363.CG Jiangxi Lianchuang, 603093.CG Nanhua Futures. (The literal RSI<40 leg 400s; fell back to oversold, which is RSI~30.)
cases.reason: Scope (China small cap) + earnings-growth + 30% drop honored, but 'RSI below 40' could not be expressed — executor 400s on any non-canonical RSI level; substituted the stricter 'oversold' (~30), so the RSI-reset threshold is off (30 not 40) and the result set is likely under-inclusive.

defects.desc: 'below'/'above' on an RSI operand 400s for non-standard levels: b='30' works (canonical oversold) but b='40' returns HTTP 400 instead of snapping to the nearest supported level + note (the schema promises snapping behavior for indicator operands). Forces a fallback to fixed-level oversold.

cases.question: Which dividend growers in Europe — raising their payout and yielding over 3% — recently reclaimed their 50-day moving average after a dip?

args.q: raising dividend growing payout every year

q: reclaimed the 50-day moving average after a dip

cases.result_summary: count=0. Fundamental leg (dps growth + yield>3%) yields only 1 European name (FirstGroup) even with the looser 'not_declining' pattern; it did not reclaim its 50-day, so the intersect is empty. TA leg alone in Europe = 40 names.
cases.reason: Query correctly built and both legs applied, but the dividend-growth (dps) fundamental leg has near-zero European coverage (1 name), so the intersect is legitimately empty — no dividend-grower + 50-day-reclaim names surface.

defects.desc: dps (dividend-per-share) history coverage for European listings appears extremely thin: dps consecutive_growth + yield>3% across 15 EU countries returns only 1 name (FirstGroup). Dividend-growth screens on Europe effectively cannot be satisfied.
When count=0 the tool still echoes a non-empty 'results' buffer (unrelated tickers), which can mislead a caller into thinking there were matches. Empty intersect should return an empty results array.
